incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency spike detected for customer 'Orion' on streaming endpoint /v1/generate-stream (region: us-west-2). p95=420ms -> 1.1s, p99=880ms -> 6.7s. Error rate stable. Auto-escalating to on-call.
Anna: I’m on-call. Jumping in. Maya can you confirm customer impact? Maya: Customer reports intermittent stalls in live transcription sessions, some users saw multi-second stalls. They flagged during a busy demo at 10:22 PDT.
Sam: Stack hint: sustained concurrency from Orion single-tenant pool spiked to 4.2k concurrent reqs, unusual long-prefix prompts (customer uses long system messages ~15k tokens).
Priya: Observed streaming stalls with backpressure in our async writer. Logs show repeated "write timeout" from stream-flush at the runtime layer. Attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T17:22:11Z] stream_flush timeout after 300ms, kv_cache_hit=false, inflight_tokens=256
[2026-03-14T17:22:12Z] connection reset by peer while muxing
```
Evan: Model-level metrics: KV cache miss rate spiked from 12% -> 67% for their sessions. Long prefixes + many concurrent sessions causing KV thrash. Likely eviction churn.
Jamie: Customer-facing: Orion is on Dedicated. They have an active contract but this is impacting real-time product demos — high priority.
Anna: Immediate actions: 1) Reduce per-tenant concurrency cap for Orion to 600 (temporary) 2) Enable degraded-mode fallback to gpt-lite-stream (lower memory) 3) Tell customer we’re investigating and mitigating.
Sam: I’ll push a soft QPS throttle on the tenant routing rule. Command:
```
# apply soft throttle
rbctl tenant set-orion --concurrency-cap 600 --reason "mitigate p99 spike"
```
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: tenant-config-updates v2026.03.14-0742 by Sam — rollout to us-west-2.
Priya: Also taking two nodes out of the autoscale pool to let KV entries stabilize (drain + restart). Will coordinate with Sam for rolling restarts of runtime pods on the dedicated pool.
Evan: Suggest enabling prefix-KV sticky caching for their sessions (experimental) to pin long prefixes to warm shards. I can flip a flag for only their tenant.
Anna: Go ahead Evan. Activate only for Orion.
Evan: Done: prefix_sticky_cache=true for tenant=orion. Monitoring effects on cache hit rate.
Maya: I’ve messaged Orion support lead to say we’ve applied temporary throttles and a fallback model; we’ll follow up with timeline within 30 minutes.
Jamie: Customer asked if this is related to their new prompt template — told them yes, long system messages + concurrency exacerbate tail-latency; we’re recommending shorter system prompts + explicit truncation if possible.
Priya: p95/p99 after throttle+sticky-cache: p95=320ms, p99=1.1s at 5m window. Much better but still above target for streaming tail. Continued monitoring.
Sam: Keeping one mitigator: enable streaming chunk-size cap to 256 tokens to avoid huge flushes. Command:
```
rbctl runtime set --stream-chunk-max 256 --tenant orion
```
Anna: Good. After 12m the incident is stabilizing. Log aggregates uploaded: https://s3.redwood-internal/incident/2330123456/logs.tar.gz
Evan: Note: root cause hypothesis: long constant prefixes cause repeated KV cache fills and eviction storms under bursty concurrency. Permanent fix options: increase KV shard memory for dedicated pools OR enforce prefix-length soft limits in routing layer.
Maya: Customer accepted temporary mitigations; wants post-incident writeup and recommended config changes.
Anna: Next steps: 1) Formal RCA draft (Evan + Priya) 2) Post-incident customer notes (Maya + Jamie) 3) Follow-up plan with infra for config and quota guardrails (Sam). I'll convert to a proper incident doc and schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow.
Jamie: Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will reopen if p99 > 2s in next 30m.
incident-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity=high, commander=Anna, created_at=2330123456, updated_at=2330123799.
